title: Veggie burger on bun with cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A veggie burger on a bun with cheese is a plant‑based patty made from a blend of legumes, vegetables and spices, served in a soft bun and topped with melted cheese. It offers a tasty alternative to a traditional meat burger while keeping the juiciness and flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Plant‑based burgers often contain up to 20 g of protein per serving.
The cheese used can be regular dairy cheese or vegan cheese made from nuts or soy.
Burger buns are frequently made from whole‑grain flour, increasing fiber content.
Veggie burgers are often grilled to add a smoky aroma without animal fats.
Choosing a veggie burger can reduce the carbon footprint compared with a beef counterpart.

items.title: High plant protein
items.content: Legume‑based patties provide a complete amino acid profile, supporting muscle maintenance and metabolism.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Vegetable ingredients and whole‑grain bun aid digestion and promote satiety.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with a beef burger, the plant version contains less saturated fat, benefiting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Legumes and whole grains supply vitamin B6 and folate, important for energy production and blood formation.

items.title: Helps lower cholesterol
items.content: Absence of animal fats and presence of plant sterols can help maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Soy or pea protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to soy or pea proteins used in the patty.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Pre‑made veggie patties can be high in salt; check the label if you watch sodium intake.

items.title: Gluten presence
items.content: The bun typically contains wheat, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite being plant‑based, the burger can be calorie‑rich due to cheese and sauces.

items.title: Texture differences
items.content: Some eaters may need time to adjust to the denser texture of a plant patty versus meat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the patty on a skillet or grill, place it in a split bun, add melted cheese, lettuce, tomato, onion and your favorite sauce. Serve immediately while the bun is soft and the cheese is stretchy.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked patties in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Frozen patties last up to 2 months; thaw them in the fridge before cooking. Store buns in a cool, dry place or in a bag at room temperature for up to 5 days.
